hist-med-01-c1.text: Yale University, Open Yale Courses (Paul Freedman, HIST 210). Lecture 19 - Charlemagne (HIST 210, The Early Middle Ages, 284-1000). Open Yale Courses, Yale University.
hist-med-01-c1.quote: Charlemagne, crowned emperor in Rome by Pope Leo III in 800, made strides in reestablishing the Roman Empire
hist-med-01-c1.claim: In 800 CE, Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne, King of the Franks, Emperor of the Romans.

hist-med-04-c3.text: Britannica Editors (1998). Gerard of Cremona. Encyclopedia Britannica.
hist-med-04-c3.quote: was a European medieval scholar who translated the works of many major Greek and Arabic writers into Latin.
hist-med-04-c3.claim: Christian scholars came to translate Arabic texts into Latin.

hist-med-06-c1.text: Britannica Editors (1998). Hagia Sophia. Encyclopedia Britannica.
hist-med-06-c1.quote: It was built as an Eastern Orthodox church between 532 and 537 ce under the direction of the Byzantine emperor Justinian I.

hist-med-02-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2018). First Crusade. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-02-c2.quote: On 27 November 1095, Urban II called for a crusade in a speech during the Council of Clermont, France.
hist-med-02-c2.claim: In 1095, Pope Urban II called upon European knights to recapture Jerusalem, then under Seljuk Turkish control, promising spiritual rewards.

hist-med-02-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2018). First Crusade. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-02-c2.quote: Conceived by Pope Urban II following an appeal from the Byzantine emperor Alexios I Komnenos, the Crusade was a success with Christian forces taking control of Jerusalem on 15 July 1099.
hist-med-02-c2.claim: Thousands responded in the First Crusade, which captured Jerusalem in 1099.

hist-med-02-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2018). Saladin. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-02-c3.quote: Saladin (1137-93) was the Muslim Sultan of Egypt and Syria (r. 1174-1193) who shocked the western world by defeating an army of the Christian Crusader states at the Battle of Hattin and then capturing Jerusalem in 1187.
hist-med-02-c3.claim: Saladin (Salah ad-Din, 1137–1193) united Egypt and Syria, recaptured Jerusalem in 1187, and became a symbol of chivalry even in Christian Europe: his magnanimity to defeated Crusaders was widely noted.

hist-med-03-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Genghis Khan. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-03-c1.quote: As his army swelled to ever greater proportions, Temujin defeated, over a period of ten years or so, such rivals as the Tartars, Kereyids, Naimans, and Merkids until a Mongol confederation met at a great conference or kurultai at the Kerulen river in 1206 and formally declared Temujin their leader.
hist-med-03-c1.claim: Temüjin, born around 1162, unified the feuding Mongol tribes and proclaimed himself Genghis Khan ('Universal Ruler') in 1206.

hist-med-03-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Black Death. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-03-c3.quote: The Black Death of 1347 entered Europe, probably via Sicily, when it was carried there by four Genoese grain ships sailing from Caffa, on the Black Sea.
hist-med-03-c3.claim: The Black Death, bubonic plague caused by Yersinia pestis, arrived in Sicily in 1347 via Genoese trading ships from the Black Sea.

hist-med-03-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Black Death. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-03-c3.quote: Sometimes entire cities, for example, Milan, managed to avoid significant effects, while others, such as Florence, were devastated - the Italian city losing 50,000 of its 85,000 population (Boccaccio claimed the impossible figure of 100,000).
hist-med-03-c3.claim: Florence lost perhaps 50–60% of its residents.

hist-med-05-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2020). Hundred Years' War. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-05-c1.quote: The Hundred Years' War (1337-1453) was an intermittent conflict between England and France lasting 116 years.
hist-med-05-c1.claim: the Hundred Years' War (1337–1453) between England and France

hist-med-05-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2019). Joan of Arc. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-05-c1.quote: Joan of Arc (Jeanne D'Arc, l. c. 1412-1431 CE) was a medieval peasant who, claiming to receive visions from God, turned the tide of the Hundred Years' War in favor of a French victory.
hist-med-05-c1.claim: Joan of Arc (1412–1431), a peasant girl who claimed divine visions, led French armies to a series of victories and helped turn the tide of the Hundred Years' War

hist-med-05-c2.text: Zain Khokhar (2020). Mehmed II. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-05-c2.quote: Thus, 29 May 1453 CE marked the fall of Constantinople.
hist-med-05-c2.claim: in 1453 Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire

hist-med-07-c2.quote: Established in 1209, the University is rich in history.
hist-med-07-c2.claim: Medieval universities (Bologna (~1088), Paris (~1150), Oxford (~1167), Cambridge (1209)) emerged as new institutions.

hist-med-07-c3.text: Joshua J. Mark (2022). Johannes Gutenberg. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-07-c3.quote: By 1450, however, his press was in operation and the first work printed is thought to have been a poem, “The Sibyl’s Prophecy”, produced through Gutenberg’s invention of movable type.
hist-med-07-c3.claim: Printing: Gutenberg's movable-type press (~1450) revolutionized communication.

hist-med-08-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Black Death. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-08-c1.quote: The Black Death of 1347 entered Europe, probably via Sicily, when it was carried there by four Genoese grain ships sailing from Caffa, on the Black Sea.
hist-med-08-c1.claim: The Black Death (bubonic and pneumonic plague) reached Europe in 1347 via Genoese ships from Crimea.

hist-med-08-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2020). Hundred Years' War. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-med-08-c2.quote: The Hundred Years' War (1337-1453) was an intermittent conflict between England and France lasting 116 years.
hist-med-08-c2.claim: The Hundred Years' War between England and France (1337-1453)
